Subject: Production and UAT latency spikes + 5xx — seeing huge queueing

Logan / Marissa —

We started seeing a large increase in tail latency and a spike in 5xx errors across our production traffic and the UAT cluster at ~08:45 PT. Impact: ~12% of requests in prod returned 5xx within a 30m window; median latency up from 120ms to ~950ms for token-gen routes. Our SREs pulled traces and it looks correlated with queued token generation on the reserved capacity pool assigned to our account.

This is blocking a customer release tonight and causing severe user-facing errors. Can you confirm whether this is a scheduling/oversubscription issue on your side or something in our integration? We need an urgent bridge and concrete mitigation plan (we can accept temporary throttles).

I've attached a short SLO extract and a couple of traces. Please escalate if you need exec attention.

—Samir

Immediate next steps (we will action now):
- 09:25 PT: Infra bridge (David + ops) to confirm pool headroom and trigger emergency scale / spillover if safe.
- 09:40 PT: Customer-facing update from Marissa with expected ETA and mitigation plan.
- If confirmed reserved-pool saturation: request for one-time burst (5x) for 2 hours and toggle to fallback model variant with lower memory/latency profile while we investigate.

I'm looping David and Hannah to lead infra diagnostics. Will update on the bridge and escalate to execs if the burst is necessary.

From: david.kim@redwood.ai

Date: 2028-05-16T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production and UAT latency spikes + 5xx — probe findings + attached profiles

Bridge notes / quick findings from initial probe (09:30 PT):

Observations:
- GPU pool assigned to TrueNorth shows sustained utilization at 94–98% on a subset of nodes; queue depth on their tenant slice increased ~6x at the spike timestamp.
- Kernel-level profile (attached: kernel-profile.csv) shows disproportionate time in attention kernel on longer sequences for the 2nd model shard.
- KV-cache churn: TTL and cache eviction traces show a heavy write/read pattern starting ~08:30 that aligns with UAT synthetic tests.
- No infra-wide outage; this is localized to the reserved pool and correlated with TrueNorth tenant slices and one co-located customer that had a large batch job.

Immediate mitigations executed (09:32–09:40 PT):
1) We enabled temporary throttles on large-batch ingestion routes for the co-located tenant to reduce KV thrash (applied at infra level).
2) Hotfix: we started an emergency 2-hour burst of additional nodes (burst request flow) but it's pending exec approval for cost authorization beyond soft limits — this is a live spot pool we can bring up in 90–120s once approved.
3) Fallback path: we can flip TrueNorth's production traffic to the lower-memory model variant (quantized) with ~10–20% quality delta but immediate 3x headroom improvement.

Recommended next actions (for approval / customer comms):
- Approve short burst (2 hours) to stabilize production while infra does root cause analysis; cost estimate: $1.9k for the 2-hour burst.
- Authorize temporary per-tenant throttles for UAT to stop synthetic test bleed into prod reserved slices.
- If TrueNorth approves, schedule a controlled canary to route 5–10% traffic to the quantized fallback to validate behaviour (30m).

I've attached the kernel profile and a short SLO PDF (slo-latency-20280516.pdf) for the timeline. Will capture full logs and propose a post-mortem after stabilization.

—David Kim
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
